A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedCBDR research despite the changed title and author list. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable throughout, including v2's Appendix A and checklist. v1 ends after its references and has no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original FCIL experiments on CIFAR10, CIFAR100 and TinyImageNet, including baseline comparisons, ablations, sensitivity analyses and visual case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds appendix results for ten clients, local training epochs, replay budgets and final-model accuracy across tasks.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the same GDR sampling procedure, TTS loss and training equations. Appendix Algorithm 1 documents the existing procedure in pseudocode; it does not establish a redesigned method or new component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate class-incremental image classification on CIFAR10, CIFAR100 and TinyImageNet. The appendix varies client counts, training budgets and analysis granularity within this retained coverage; it introduces no new dataset, domain or task requirement.

E2.justification: The original six-baseline comparisons remain unchanged. The added ten-client comparisons in Tables 6–7 omit Finetune, while Table 8's replay-budget comparison includes only Re-Fed, omitting LANDER from the corresponding Table 4 comparator set. No new named baseline is introduced.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the evaluation settings with ten-client comparisons and local-epoch sweeps over 1, 2, 5 and 10 epochs. Appendix A.3.6 adds final-task evaluation using 50 communication rounds and a 150-sample CIFAR10 replay budget, compared with 100 rounds and 450 samples in the original three-task setup. The original experiments remain intact.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds local-training sensitivity analysis and final-model task breakdowns that examine optimization robustness and retention of earlier classes. It also extends replay-budget sensitivity to ten clients and class-distribution analysis to CIFAR100 with ten tasks. These supplement the unchanged original ablations and case studies.

E5.justification: The original three-seed mean and standard-deviation reporting remains unchanged. New Tables 6–7 explicitly report results using the single fixed seed 2023, without uncertainty estimates. This adds seed-specific reporting, not additional repeated-run evidence for the original results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the original empirical figures retain their results, while Tables 6–9 and Figures 7–9 add substantial new findings. For example, Table 6 reports 59.80% for FedCBDR versus 48.24% for FedLwF on CIFAR10 with three tasks, ten clients and beta=0.5. These are newly reported results under additional settings, not improvements over the earlier five-client scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup and equations 1–9 are retained. The appendix adds pseudocode and empirical material, but no new formal assumptions, definitions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same GDR/TTS contributions, class-balancing and forgetting claims, and reported 2%–15% Top-1 accuracy advantage over six baselines. The additional appendix evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3.5 adds an interpretation linking longer local training to biased updates and attributing greater stability to TTS. A.3.6 interprets task-level results in terms of LANDER's forgetting and the retention benefits of GDR/TTS. Existing limitations concerning transmission costs, hyperparameter sensitivity and globally imbalanced data remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds Algorithm 1, dataset statistics in Table 5, appendix experiment details and statements about supplementary code. It explicitly specifies 10,240 synthetic samples per task for TARGET as well as LANDER in the appendix comparison. Original backbone, optimizer, hyperparameter ranges and GPU details remain unchanged; actual code availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The bibliography expands from 39 to 54 entries, adding works such as FedSSA and SR-FDIL and removing some earlier citations, including the original Grad-CAM reference. These changes alter the citation base, but the related-work taxonomy and FedCBDR's positioning relative to exemplar replay, generative replay and distillation remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and author/affiliation block change, and v2 adds appendix cross-references, Appendix A and a NeurIPS checklist. The main prose and section sequence are largely retained, so the revision does not constitute extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 changes from a two-column ACM layout to a single-column NeurIPS layout, resizing and repositioning retained figures and tables. It adds Algorithm 1, Tables 5–9 and Figures 7–9. Figure 7 introduces a caption error: its caption describes replay-buffer class counts although the figure displays accuracy curves.

improvement.justification: The added ten-client comparisons, local-epoch sensitivity study and final-task breakdown provide useful empirical checks absent from v1, while pseudocode and dataset statistics improve documentation. These are incremental gains: the core method, main results and limitations remain unchanged, and single-seed appendix comparisons plus Figure 7's incorrect caption limit the strength and clarity of the added evidence.
